answer: Yarrow-Jitter Admission: each agent derives a per-window timing kernel from a public yarrow beacon and its own clock drift, then schedules requests as a bounded-burst renewal process anchored to that kernel. Ingress compares each identity’s inter-arrival distribution to the expected shape and tests cross-identity correlation. Sybils from one orchestrator share a timing anchor, yielding low entropy or synchronized bursts; they are throttled. To pass, an attacker must run independent clocks, jitter sources, and egress paths per identity, raising coordination cost and cutting throughput.
